evidence.source: CASE報科學 (National Taiwan University Center for Science Education)
evidence.text: The author identifies rare, damaged Shang oracle-bone forms as 能 and describes a bear-like pictograph: the head is reduced to an eye-shaped form, the limbs become more linear, and the short tail remains. The author says the few oracle-bone occurrences are too damaged to establish their use. From oracle bone to Western Zhou bronze, the head changes from an eye-like shape to 㠯, the body is simplified to 月 (肉), and the feet are rearranged side by side; the later bronze, Warring States, Chu-slip, Qin-slip, seal, and clerical forms are described as easier to relate. This conflicts with another paleographic account that considers securely identified 能 earliest in Western Zhou bronze; the Shang identification is therefore disputed, not settled.
evidence.title: 獼猴與黑熊：甲骨文的「夒」、「猱」與「能」

evidence.source: 劉雲, Fudan University Center for Unearthed Documents and Ancient Chinese Characters
evidence.text: The author says securely identifiable 能 in ancient writing first appears in Western Zhou bronze inscriptions, and argues a disputed Shang animal-shaped graph is not 能 but 鷧, a cormorant: it differs in the supposed bear's neck, feet, tail, and head. The article's discussion establishes a material disagreement over whether a Shang form is 能; the identification remains contested. It supplies images of Western Zhou examples including 能匋尊, 鬲比簋, 毛公厝鼎, and 番生簋, but the web text does not provide a dated first inscription.
evidence.title: 劉雲：釋“鷧”及相關諸字

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》, text hosted by Wikisource
evidence.field: 卷十, 能部; entry for 能
evidence.text: The Han dictionary defines 能 as a kind of bear with feet like a deer, analyzes it as 从肉㠯聲, and explains 賢能 and 能傑 through the animal's firmness and strength. This is the Shuowen's account, not independent confirmation that the 㠯-shaped part was historically phonetic: later graphic analysis associates that shape with the head in the bear pictograph.
evidence.title: 說文解字/10

evidence.source: Kotobank, entry 能 (デジタル大辞泉等 reference aggregation)
evidence.text: The entry reports an early Western Zhou bronze use in which 能 functions as a verb meaning ‘be able to’ (citing 周初金文), and a use in 詩經·大雅·民勞 glossed ‘soften the harsh and govern the near’; it says the ‘talent/ability’ sense appears in later Warring States-era texts such as 左傳. It also records 能 for ‘bear’ in a variant reading of 左傳·昭公七年. These cited examples support ability use by Western Zhou/early classical textual evidence and bear use in a transmitted Zuozhuan variant, but they do not by themselves establish a linear semantic chronology or how bear and ability senses are historically connected.
evidence.kind: dictionary report of cited historical attestations
evidence.title: 能(ノウ)とは？ 意味や使い方

No separate sound component is proposed by the supported early graphic analysis; 㠯 in the Shuowen segmentation is disputed as phonetic because it plausibly reflects the altered bear head.

gaps: The earliest graph is disputed: NTU's article identifies damaged Shang oracle-bone forms as 能 but says their use cannot be determined; Liu Yun argues securely identifiable 能 begins in Western Zhou bronze and reidentifies a disputed Shang shape as 鷧. The accessible text cannot settle this paleographic disagreement.

No dated inscription citation establishing the earliest secure bear-word use was recovered. A dictionary report cites early Western Zhou bronze for verbal 能 ‘be able’ and later classical sources, but semantic links between the bear noun and ability are not established by those examples.

Shuowen's 㠯 phonetic analysis is historically important but likely reflects a reinterpretation of the head's transformed shape; no independently established sound-component role is supported here. No separate meaningful semantic and phonetic components should be asserted for the earliest pictograph.

No ancient pronunciation or spoken name for the depicted bear is independently recovered; no borrowing claim between an object's name and a pronoun/ability word is supported or needed by the reviewed accounts.

The direct official Unihan character URL https://www.unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=80FD could not be inspected, despite the local kMandarin row néng. Its required official character-specific click-through verification remains incomplete.
No matching component graph with independently verified readings was established, so there is no valid component sound-array comparison.
